relevance.rationale: This paper addresses, by name, an analytic debt the corpus has explicitly recorded as unformalised. QOU/Archimedean/AwZeroLocalization.lean opens: 'The KSel-2-ID chain's remaining analytic debt (TropicalClassTransport §3, the u1-promotion audit §4 gap 2) is the zero asymptotics of the Ramanujan entire function (q-Airy function) A_w(z) = Sum_{m>=0} w^{m^2}(-z)^m/(w;w)_m', proved in docs/audits/2026-08-01-awzero-asymptotics.md 'by recentring A_w at index n, identifying the limit of the recentred series as a Jacobi theta function whose zero set is the lattice w^{2Z}, and running Rouche against that theta limit', with the note that 'the analytic steps that need complex analysis (Jacobi triple product, Rouche, the argument principle) are NOT formalised here'. Morita's A_q(x) := Sum_{n>=0} q^{n^2}(-x)^n/(q;q)_n (§3.1) is character-for-character the same function, under the same hypothesis 0 < |q| < 1. His main theorem is an EXACT identity writing A_{q^2} as a Jacobi-theta-weighted combination of two q-Airy functions — i.e. a published, exact version of the theta comparison the corpus's audit builds by hand — and his own stated motivation is that 'our new relation shows an asymptotic behavior of the Ramanujan function near the infinity'. Independently corroborating: the corpus's existing ismail2005qairy entry carries the note 'No zero-asymptotics theorem is attributed to it', so the corpus knows it lacks a source for exactly this. The paper also sits inside the q-Borel/q-Laplace framework of Zhang that QOU/MathlibExt/QBorelKernel.lean already builds on.

keyResults.statement: For all x in C*, A_{q^2}(-q^3/x^2) = (1/(q,-1;q)_infinity) * { theta(x/q) Ai_q(-x) + theta(-x/q) Ai_q(x) }, where theta is the Jacobi theta function and Ai_q the q-Painleve q-Airy function.
keyResults.useForFolio: An exact closed-form theta factorisation of the Ramanujan function A_q, valid for all x in C*. The corpus's Rouche argument compares A_w against a theta LIMIT obtained by recentring; this identity is the exact statement that comparison approximates, so the zero asymptotics zeta_n = w^{1-2n}(1 + O(w^n)) can be read off the theta zero lattice with the error controlled by the Ai_q factors rather than by a hand-built limit. Hypotheses check out: 0 < |q| < 1 matches the corpus's 0 < w < 1 (set q^2 = w), and the series definitions coincide exactly.

keyResults.statement: A_q satisfies the q-difference equation (q x sigma_q^2 - sigma_q + 1) u(x) = 0, whose second solution is u(x) = theta(x) * 2phi_0(0,0;-;q,-x) with the 2phi_0 series DIVERGENT.
keyResults.useForFolio: Shows the theta function is intrinsic to the q-difference equation A_q solves — it is the multiplier attached to the divergent second solution, not an artefact of a chosen comparison. That is the structural reason the corpus's theta-limit step works, and it is the level-1 q-Borel kernel picture (t_n = q^{n(n-1)/2}) that QBorelKernel.lean already formalises, now instantiated on a function the corpus actually uses.

keyResults.statement: Jacobi's triple product identity: theta(x) = (q, -x, -q/x; q)_infinity.
keyResults.useForFolio: Exactly one of the three analytic steps AwZeroLocalization.lean names as not formalised ('Jacobi triple product, Rouche, the argument principle'). Having it stated with the paper's own normalisation removes the normalisation ambiguity when that step is eventually formalised or cited.

proposedActions.rationale: Orphan. The corpus already registers ismail2005qairy (which names A_q but proves no zero asymptotics) and ramis-sauloy-zhang2013 (the q-Borel framework); this is the missing middle term. Suggested id morita2011qairy — note references.ts already carries morita1981 and morita1982 for Katsusada Morita, a DIFFERENT author; do not collide.

Hypotheses verified to hold, not merely 'related': the paper's A_q is the corpus's A_w term-for-term, and its standing assumption 0 < |q| < 1 is satisfied. The identity supplies the exact theta-factorised form of A_q at infinity that the audit's recentring argument constructs approximately. SCOPE, stated honestly: it does not by itself yield zeta_n = w^{1-2n}(1 + O(w^n)) — the argument-principle/Rouche step against the theta zero lattice still has to be run — but it replaces the hand-built theta limit with a published exact identity, which is the part of the debt that is currently unbacked.

Evaluate both sides of the Theorem numerically at the substrate-relevant w and a spread of x, and check the zeros predicted by the theta factor against the tropical corners w^{1-2n} the probe computes. A mismatch would indicate the corpus's normalisation of A_w differs from Morita's; agreement independently validates the refuted-triangulation-free style of check the audit currently lacks.
